stories.title: Dow erases a 1,100-point drop to close +0.34%; S&P 500 −0.25%, Nasdaq −0.62%
stories.body: Stocks finished mostly lower but well off their lows: the S&P 500 fell 0.25%, the Nasdaq 0.62% and the Dow eked out a 0.34% gain (TipRanks). At the session lows the Nasdaq was down as much as 4.6%, the S&P 500 3.2% and the Dow 2.2%; by 3:27 PM ET the S&P 500 was −0.2%, the Nasdaq −0.6% and the Dow up 287 points (+0.6%) (Beinsure). CNBC reported the Dow closed higher after wiping out a 1,100-point loss. Reuters said bargain hunters stepped in ahead of Thanksgiving; Beinsure cited light trading and a Michael Burry post saying his portfolio was "temporarily almost entirely long." SPY ended at $717.27 (−0.21%) and QQQ at $633.81 (−0.67%) at the 4:00 PM ET print, after lows of −3.24% and −4.75% (Structure One feed).
stories.why: SPY's completed 1-hour closes climbed from $699.06 (11:00 AM candle) to $717.27 and QQQ's from $610.41 to $633.81, yet none closed above Tuesday's close; Friday's 1:00 PM close leaves four hourly candles before the weekend.

stories.title: Meta +3.4% bucks the slide; Amazon −3.2% on an AWS traffic note
stories.body: At the 4:00 PM ET print META was +3.39%, AMZN −3.19%, GOOG −2.08% and MSFT −1.29% (Structure One feed). JournalArta tied Meta's gain to a reported $4.5 billion GPU-backed CoreWeave loan for a Meta data center in Georgia and to talks with Amazon about restoring access for its Muse shopping agent. MoneyCheck cited a Bernstein note that web activity at usage-based cloud platforms, including AWS, ran about 16% below Q3 levels in mid-to-late November.
stories.why: Megacaps split sharply within the same session; completed 1-hour closes show which names held the afternoon rebound.

stories.title: Chips claw back: Micron trims a 13% drop to 4%, AMD to 1.6%
stories.body: Chip stocks recovered most of their morning losses: at the 4:00 PM ET print MU was −4.07% (low −12.97%), AMD −1.56% (low −10.37%), INTC −0.66% (low −10.31%) and AVGO −0.20% (low −7.67%) (Structure One feed). The semiconductor index was −1.3% around 3:05 PM ET (Reuters) after falling more than 6% earlier (Yahoo Finance). Lam Research was −5.96% (Reuters), and Ambarella fell more than 19% after weak guidance (Beinsure).
stories.why: Intraday ranges of 8–13% kept chip implied volatility high; only completed 1-hour closes separated the morning flush from the recovery.

stories.title: Energy leads late as oil rises; banks recover to flat
stories.body: Materials, energy and real estate each rose more than 1% in the afternoon (Beinsure). At the 4:00 PM ET print CVX was +1.27%, XOM +0.14%, JPM +0.09% and BAC +0.04%, after BAC fell as much as 3.34% and JPM 2.40% in the morning (Structure One feed). WTI was up 2% at $83.65 in afternoon trading (The Library).
stories.why: Banks round-tripped a 2–3% drop inside one session, while energy tracked crude; hourly closes show which move held into the close.

stories.title: Nvidia ends −3.9% after an intraday drop of more than 9%
stories.body: Nvidia ended at $149.29 (−3.92%) at the 4:00 PM ET print after touching $141.17 (−9.15%) in the morning, versus Tuesday's $155.38 close (Structure One feed); Reuters had it −4.7% around 3:05 PM ET. Yahoo Finance tied the drop to worries about AI profitability and overinvestment. Huang was reinstated as CEO on Monday, and his congressional appearance next week is in focus (The Library).
stories.why: A second straight down session with a 9% intraday range; completed 1-hour closes filter the swings that intraday prints exaggerate.

stories.title: Gold ETF turns positive after a 3.5% drop; silver ETF recovers 6%
stories.body: GLD ended at $327.47 (+0.62%) and SLV at $37.12 (+0.76%) at the 4:00 PM ET print, after morning lows of −3.53% and −6.41% (Structure One feed). Gold futures were down 0.6% at $3,540 in the afternoon (The Library). 24/7 Wall St. said gold is having its worst November since at least 2000, citing Fed hike odds and forced selling during the tech selloff.
stories.why: Metals sold off with stocks in the morning and recovered with them; GLD and SLV hourly closes show whether that link persists.

stories.title: Oil climbs 2% with Hormuz shipping risk and the tariff plan in focus
stories.body: WTI was up 2% at $83.65 in afternoon trading (The Library). IC Markets cited reports of further attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, and Saxo noted Iran said four tankers hit mines there. Separately, the USTR proposed Section 301 tariffs on 14 economies, up to 35% on Vietnam, 20% on China and 15% on the EU, with comments due Jan. 5, 2027 (StockTitan). USO ended +3.29% and OXY +1.24% at the 4:00 PM ET print (Structure One feed).
stories.why: Shipping and trade headlines can gap oil-linked names across the Thursday closure; OXY and USO hourly closes show how they absorb them.

stories.title: VIX eases to about 28 after topping 35 in the morning
stories.body: The VIX reached 35 in the morning and was up 6% at 28 in the afternoon (The Library); Yahoo Finance's quote bar showed 27.83 (+5.57%) about an hour before the close. Early Wednesday, Saxo noted December VIX futures at 24.40 with the term structure in backwardation.
stories.why: A VIX near 28 keeps premiums elevated into a holiday week whose short-dated options span Thursday's closure and Friday's early close.

stories.title: 10-year yield eases to 4.85% as 98% hike odds hold
stories.body: The 10-year Treasury yield was 4.85% in the afternoon, down from Tuesday's 4.93% close (The Library); earlier it was 4.82%, down 7 bp (Yahoo Finance). Traders priced a 98% chance of a 25 bp hike at the December meeting (Yahoo Finance). Freddie Mac's 30-year fixed mortgage rate fell to 7.21% from 7.28% (Yahoo Finance).
stories.why: Lower yields with a near-certain hike priced point to growth worries; yield moves can shift index ETFs within one hourly candle.

stories.title: Europe closes lower, DAX −1.23%; Asia led the chip slump
stories.body: The DAX closed −1.23% at 24,710, the CAC 40 −0.62% at 7,991 and the FTSE 100 −0.32% at 10,434 as AI-valuation worries and US tariff plans weighed, with Infineon the DAX's biggest decliner (Trading Economics). Earlier the KOSPI closed −6.16% and the Nikkei −2.78% (Trading Economics), as Asian chip stocks slumped on AI doubts (Al Jazeera).
stories.why: Europe closed before the US rebound, so overseas markets reopen with that recovery still to price in, adding gap risk.

stories.title: Core PCE 3.3% beats; Q3 GDP 4.3%; new home sales at a 701,000 pace
stories.body: October PCE rose 3.8% y/y as forecast; core 3.3% vs 3.2% expected (Yahoo Finance, SSBCrack). Q3 GDP second estimate 4.3% vs 3.4% advance and 3.5% forecast (BEA, XTB). Claims fell to 189,000 vs 200,000 expected (Rallies). October new home sales came in at a 701,000 annual rate (StockTitan).
stories.why: The 8:30 AM data showed up in the opening gap, not inside an hourly candle.

stories.title: Nvidia ends just under the $150 strike that led Tuesday's options volume
stories.body: Longbridge counted 4,633,214 NVDA contracts Tuesday, 55% calls; the top contract was the Nov. 25 $150 put (182,925). NVDA ended at $149.29 at the 4:00 PM ET print, just below that strike, after trading as low as $141.17 (Structure One feed).
stories.why: Heavy volume at a strike expiring today can add to swings near it into the bell; reported activity, not a signal.

stories.title: Ahead: market shut Thursday, 1:00 PM close Friday; OPEC+ meets Nov. 29
stories.body: US markets are closed Thursday for Thanksgiving and reopen Friday for a half day, closing at 1:00 PM ET (Yahoo Finance, The Library). OPEC+ ministers meet Nov. 29 (Saxo). Jensen Huang's congressional appearance next week is in focus (The Library). Broadcom reports Dec. 9 (Broadcom IR), and the December Fed meeting is priced for a 25 bp hike (Yahoo Finance).
stories.why: Friday's shortened session gives only a few completed hourly closes, with gap risk across Thursday and the weekend.
